canonical_definition: World Knowledge refers to the broad, factual, and domain-specific knowledge embedded in pre-trained large language models (LLMs) or multimodal models, encompassing encyclopedic information, commonsense reasoning, and structured representations of rules or relationships. It is acquired through pretraining and applied to support downstream tasks such as question answering, inference, zero-shot reasoning, and interpretation of real-world contexts, with some definitions emphasizing its grounding in truthful facts or dynamic integration of prior and local knowledge. While some papers narrowly operationalize it via factual benchmarks (e.g., MMLU), others highlight its role in agentic tasks, visio-linguistic reasoning, or structured forms like hierarchical knowledge graphs.
